cards.weakest: Head counter. Notices exactly who hasn't said a word all week.
cards.issue: Best opener in the run: 'which one are you in the group chat' is a format people already screenshot and tag friends on. Head counter reads a little creepy and is the only line with no joke. Planner's 'I already booked it' is a small flex but everyone knows a Planner, so it survives.
cards.fix: Replace Head counter with: "Counter. Knows exactly who didn't react to MY message." (same T02B need-for-contact read, now a self-own people will admit to).

cards.weakest: Keep mine. "Ask me anything, anytime. I'll answer."
cards.issue: Great tension, and the live-location counteroffer is a real move people make. But the 'keep mine' line is the noble answer: it sounds like a therapist-approved boundary, so private people pick it to look mature instead of admitting it.
cards.fix: Rewrite to: "Keep mine. 'Nothing to hide. Still no.'" (same R1 -2, T01B 2; now it is funny and a little guilty, same charm as 'Type mine in before they finish').

cards.weakest: Cringe. This is a lot.
cards.issue: Good feeling set; 'Trapped. Saying no now would look guilty' is the most honest line in chapter 1. 'Cringe. This is a lot.' is thin next to it. Feeling cards are never shared, which is fine, but this is the first of seven cards that all ask 'what showed up first?'.
cards.fix: Change 'Cringe. This is a lot.' to "Cringe. We are not that couple." and vary the stem: "They said 'swap passcodes.' Your gut said..."

cards.weakest: Nowhere. Slept on it. It was smaller by morning.
cards.issue: Strong real card: 'Posted something vague and waited to see who'd ask' is the vaguepost confession people will laugh at in comments. The sleep-on-it line is the healthy, well-adjusted cool answer; nobody at 1am thinks that is them, but everyone wants to be it.
cards.fix: Rewrite to: "Nowhere. Stared at the ceiling till 3am, told no one." (keeps R1 -1: it stays with you, minus the wellness halo).

cards.weakest: Read the entire privacy policy first. Yes, all of it.
cards.issue: Allow-all and the 2am revoke after one scary video are both perfect. Reading the whole policy is the cool answer: nobody does it, everyone will claim it. As a reviewer I'd also clip this card if the app itself asks for broad permissions later, so the honest options matter here.
cards.fix: Replace with: "Deny everything, then hit 'only while using' when it breaks." (honest, common, T01B 1; drop the T25A tag from this card).

cards.weakest: Totally fine. Next hangout, we pick up mid-sentence.
cards.issue: Sharp this-or-that, and 'Someone should've texted. Them.' is a great self-own. The A side is the flattering 'secure friend' caption; half the people who feel B will pick A to look chill.
cards.fix: Rewrite A to: "Totally fine. I also didn't text for four months." (keeps T02A, adds the same self-roast B has).

cards.issue: Fast, true, funny. 'Leave it pending. Forever.' is a caption people will quote. Third T04 circle-size card in chapter 1, though (C1-1, C1-7, C1-10).
cards.fix: None to the lines. Keep it, and move C1-10 out of the group-chat setting (see C1-10).

cards.weakest: Send my own clumsy version, typos and all.
cards.issue: Is an AI apology still a real apology? This is comment-section gold, the kind of debate that makes people argue under a creator's video. The B line copies the tag name T03B word for word and reads a bit virtuous.
cards.fix: Rewrite B to: "Send my own version. It took 40 minutes and says sorry six times."

cards.weakest: Counteroffer: a shared playlist. Same closeness, less schedule.
cards.issue: 'Say yes, then never open it again' is the honest winner. The playlist counteroffer is too cute; it is the answer you would pick to seem emotionally intelligent.
cards.fix: Replace with: "Say yes. Keep a second calendar they don't know about." (R1 -1, funny and a little guilty).

cards.weakest: React to everything. Still know nobody by Friday.
cards.issue: Lines are funny ('Mute it before the welcome messages finish loading'), but a second group-chat card in the same chapter as C1-1 and the third T04 card reads as repeat, which is exactly what Jerry flagged in test 1.
cards.fix: Move the setting: "A wedding. You're seated at a table of ten strangers." / "Learn every name and start a group chat by dessert." / "Text my two people: 'who ARE these people?'" / "Eat, smile, leave before the speeches." / "Toast with everyone. Remember nobody by Monday."

cards.weakest: Hum your own version of the chorus back at them.
cards.issue: Golden-set card and it still lands. 'Hum your own version' is confusing: is it a joke, a critique, a flex? It takes two reads.
cards.fix: Replace with: "'Honestly? Enter the other song you played me.'" (R2 +1, T07A 1, clear and funny).

cards.weakest: Told them it was over my budget. Suggested something cheaper.
cards.issue: 'Invented a clash. Sent a very long, very sweet message instead' is the best line in the chapter. The budget line is the financially literate cool answer, stated flat. Also 'instant noodles' shows up again in C5-2.
cards.fix: Rewrite to: "Admitted it's over my budget in the chat. Took three drafts." and change the noodles line to: "Went, paid, and lived on cereal till payday."

cards.weakest: DM your friend: "Your call. I'm with you either way."
cards.issue: Heaviest and least fun card in the chapter; the setup reads like a mediation form. The DM-your-friend line is the saintly answer. 'Keep the old screenshots, just in case' is the only line anyone would repeat.
cards.fix: Prompt: "The person who started a rumor about your friend last year wants back in the group chat. They apologized. Publicly. With a slideshow." Option: "DM my friend: 'say the word and I hit decline.'"

cards.weakest: Send a long voice note about why they're amazing.
cards.issue: 'Honestly, they were mid anyway' is screenshot material, and the six moves are genuinely different. Pick two avoids a cool answer because nobody is forced into one frame.
cards.fix: Optional punch-up: "Send a voice note listing why they're amazing. Numbered."

cards.weakest: Told them straight: that was wrong, go fix it.
cards.issue: 'Laughed along, then felt weird about it all day' is brutally honest and is why this card works. 'Told them straight' is the hero answer: people will remember themselves as braver than they were, even on a real card.
cards.fix: Rewrite to: "Told them straight it was wrong. They left me on read for two days." (same R2 +2, now it has a cost).

cards.weakest: Worried I'd get dragged into it.
cards.issue: 'Guilty. Part of me found it funny.' is the realest feeling line in the run. Fine as is, but the stem 'what showed up first?' is on its second outing of seven.
cards.fix: Vary the stem: "Rewind to that moment. First feeling, no editing."

cards.issue: Golden-set scenario plus 'third night this week', which makes it sting. 'Start a group call. Tag in a second friend.' is the funniest new move. Everyone has been on both ends of this text; people will send this card to the friend in question.
cards.fix: None.

cards.weakest: Waits till they ask, then gives the honest take.
cards.issue: 'Compliments the shoes. Says nothing about the hair.' is the most screenshot-able line in the whole quiz. The prompt is overloaded (four sentences plus a role stem), and 'waits till they ask' is the mature cool answer.
cards.fix: Prompt: "Your friend walks in with a dramatic new haircut. It's not working. Nobody asked. You're the one who..." Option: "Waits till they ask. Then says 'it's growing on me.'"

cards.weakest: Skip the loan. Help them hunt down a cheaper one tonight.
cards.issue: Six options is too many for a money card and two of them are the responsible adult answer (payback date, go deal-hunting). 'You're a disaster. Then send it anyway.' is the only line with personality. Also the third 'already has a job' phrasing in the run.
cards.fix: Cut the cheaper-laptop option. Rewrite the payback line: "Send it. Log it in my Notes app under 'owed'." (T12A 2). Circumstance line: "I can't. That money is rent."

cards.issue: Top three card. 'Make a joke about it that's clearly not a joke' is the move everyone has made. Only weakness: 'a red flag' is abstract, and the joke lives in the specific flag.
cards.fix: Name the flag: "Your friend's new crush still has their ex as their lock screen. Your friend beams: 'So?? What do you all think?'"

cards.issue: 'Show up, complain the whole way, take the heavy end' is exactly Rolls-eyes-grabs-keys energy. 'Send pizza for the helpers and a very warm text' is a perfect roast of the move. No cool answer.
cards.fix: None.

cards.weakest: Make it official, then invent our own rules for what that means.
cards.issue: Good opener energy ('mid-snack'), but 'invent our own rules for what that means' is abstract and reads like a survey item. 'Be my person?' is sweet, not funny.
cards.fix: Rewrite to: "Yes, official. Then we write our own rules. Rule one: naps." and "Say it properly: 'Be my person?' I practiced in the mirror."

cards.weakest: Introduced them around, then went off with my own friends.
cards.issue: 'Basically one person with two phones' is a perfect line and couples will send it to each other. Real card, did-grade, zero cool answer.
cards.fix: Optional: "Introduced them to everyone. Then abandoned them by the chips."

cards.weakest: One shared pot. Everything goes in, nobody keeps score.
cards.issue: 50/50 versus by-income is the most reliable comment war on the internet, so share is high. But the options are dry except the olive oil, and 'one shared pot, nobody keeps score' is the romantic cool answer. Bigger problem: T12 split fairness appears on C2-9, C3-3, C4-9 and C4-11, the exact equal-vs-proportional repeat Jerry called out in test 1.
cards.fix: Options: "50/50. I'll just buy cheaper olive oil." / "By income, so it pinches us the same." / "Separate everything. Label the olive oil." / "One pot. I will absolutely keep score." (T12B 1 becomes an honest line). Then cut C4-11.

cards.weakest: They get a play-by-play of my day, lunch included.
cards.issue: 'If they're free, I'm suddenly free too' is a sting people will tag their partner in. Solid pick two. R1 and T09 are already heavy in this chapter (C3-2, C3-4, C3-10).
cards.fix: Optional: "They get a play-by-play of my day. Photos of lunch included."

cards.weakest: Ended it kindly. Some things just don't fit.
cards.issue: 'Joked about it until they finally got the hint' is great. 'Ended it kindly' is the emotionally mature caption answer; the real version is messier.
cards.fix: Rewrite to: "Ended it with a kind text I rewrote eleven times."

cards.issue: 'Resentment. I'd been keeping quiet score.' is a devastating true line. Emotion-only card doing its job.
cards.fix: Vary the stem away from 'What showed up first?': "Back then, the feeling underneath was..."

cards.weakest: That we never said out loud what's off-limits.
cards.issue: Heavy but 'Envy. Someone else got the good version of them' is a gut-punch people will quote. The off-limits line is abstract and takes a second read.
cards.fix: Rewrite to: "That we never agreed on what counts as cheating." (teen version: "That we never said what 'best friend' means.")

cards.weakest: Someday, but only once my life feels steady.
cards.issue: 'Is a dog basically the same thing? Asking for me.' is the line people will share. 18+ locked, handled with warmth. The steady-life line is fine but plain.
cards.fix: Optional: "Someday. After I can keep a plant alive."

cards.weakest: Take it. My person carries more of the baby care at first.
cards.issue: Reads like a policy questionnaire. No joke anywhere, and the 'my person carries more' line is confusing. Locked and gated so low reach, but it still has to be fun.
cards.fix: Prompt: "You circled 'start trying' on the calendar for spring. Then your dream job calls: bigger title, way more hours." Option: "Take it. We move the circle to next spring."

cards.weakest: Ask if there's anything like it closer to home.
cards.issue: 'Say go, and quietly look forward to the quiet' is a great private sting. The closer-to-home line is honest (the clingy move said nicely), so it stays.
cards.fix: None.

cards.weakest: Skip it. We pick our own random day in March.
cards.issue: Cute and teen-safe. 'Pizza, a show, zero mention of the date' is the relatable one. The random-day-in-March line is the quirky cool-couple answer.
cards.fix: Rewrite to: "Skip it. Celebrate on the 15th when the chocolate's half off."

cards.fix: Rewrite to: "Straight into savings. It never even touched my wallet."

cards.weakest: Fair. They did work hard, and it shows.
cards.issue: Spicy, comment-bait, Sally Q13. A is the diplomatic answer that sounds nice at a party. C5-3 is the same nepotism debate one chapter later, which Jerry will notice.
cards.fix: Keep this card (it covers Q13) and steal C5-3's best line for B: "Must be nice. Somebody had to say it." A: "'You earned it!' I say, and mean it." Cut C5-3.

cards.weakest: The other pair. That $80 already has plans.

cards.fix: Prompt: "The $80-more sneakers are the pair you've watched 11 unboxing videos of." / "Buy them. I've already worn them in my head." / "Buy the cheap pair. Nobody looks at my feet."

cards.weakest: The $10 one. I'll give to causes when I choose.

cards.fix: Make it cost something: "A plant for your room: $10 at the big store, or $26 from a neighbor whose sales fund the animal shelter." / "The neighbor's. The shelter dogs deserve it." / "The $10 one. The shelter gets my likes and shares."

cards.weakest: Left it in my cart until the feeling passed.
cards.issue: 'Bought it, then hid the bag for a few days' is the confession of the chapter. The cart line is slightly virtuous but real.
cards.fix: Optional: "Left it in my cart. Checked on it like a pet."

cards.issue: 'Worry. I opened the bank app.' is funny and true.
cards.fix: Vary the stem: "Right after checkout, your gut said..."

cards.fix: Prompt: "Your group of four runs a weekend pop-up and makes $400. Same hours each. Sam's glitter phone charms sold most of it." Option: "Equal piles. Sam gets bragging rights."

cards.weakest: Venue picker. Chose the cheap spot so everyone could come.

cards.fix: Replace Venue picker with: "Bathroom break. Perfect timing, every single time." (no tag, or T12A 1 at the auditor's call).

cards.issue: Golden set. 'Watch a friend pull and scream along for free' is the best new line. Neutral on gacha, no guilt loop, so it won't get roasted by the monetization-ethics crowd.
cards.fix: None.

50 tags in 25 pairs against the brief's ~42; more names means more share-card variety but thinner triggers per tag. Several stock phrases repeat between cards and library ('already has a job', 'Future me', 'zero guilt', 'Fair is fair').
library.fix: Evidence auditor to confirm every tag has 2+ cards; sweep the repeated phrases per the card fixes above.

overall: Okay, as the guy who roasts these for a living: this is way better than a personality quiz has any right to be, and I'd actually play it on camera. The winners are the cards where the joke is the move, not the setup: the haircut 'compliments the shoes', the red-flag crush 'joke that's clearly not a joke', 'same dishes, same seats, same fight', 'one person with two phones', 'my fun money is gone by the 10th', and the Uno stacking war. Those get screenshotted and argued about in comments. Three things would get this clowned in a review. One: repetition. The 'what showed up first?' stem runs seven times, split-the-bill fairness shows up on four cards, the nepotism debate twice, the free afternoon twice, and lines like 'already has a job', 'Future me says thanks', 'zero guilt' and 'Fair is fair' reappear. Jerry's test-1 note was literally 'three of the same answers', so cut C4-11 and C5-3 and sweep the phrases. Two: cool answers. Reading the whole privacy policy, the $3 shelter plant, 'my free time is not for sale', giving away your own ticket, sleeping on it at 1am. Each is the answer people pick to look good, and each one quietly poisons the result. Every option needs a small self-own like the best ones have. Three: a few cards read like surveys (the rumor comeback, the kids-versus-job card, the swapped-roles prompt nobody can parse in one pass). The library is strong; Golden Retriever, Weighted Blanket, My passcode my dignity, Compliment sandwich chef are share-card bangers. Chill Personified, Slow-and-Steady Regular and Soft-Spoken Rebel are the ones nobody posts. And drop the 'ask Genii a follow-up' call: predictions that sell the app are exactly what I'd put in a dark-patterns segment.
